Issued at 230 PM EDT Thu Sep 24 2026

Current-Friday...A weak "cool" frontal boundary continues to sag 
into the southern FL peninsula thru late day and early evening. 
Mostly SCT onshore-moving showers and ISOLD lightning storms will
remain possible thru the afternoon and early evening with chances
confined closer towards the coast later this evening and
overnight. Breezy/windy/gusty northerly winds will gradually 
fall to around 10 mph or less inland this evening and overnight, 
but may remain elevated 15-20 mph along the immediate
Volusia/Space coasts with frequent higher gusts as the pgrad 
remains rather tight. Primary impacts from convection remain heavy
downpours, brief gusty winds and occasional lightning strikes. 
With drier air filtering down the peninsula precip chances into 
Fri (20-50%) will mostly remain confined closer towards the coast 
as activity moves southward. Northerly winds will remain stout 
again on Fri, with speeds 15-20 mph (10-15 mph well inland) and 
gusts 25-30 mph (highest toward the coast). 

These persistent, strong northerly winds have created life-
threatening beach and marine conditions. Dangerous rip currents and 
rough surf will continue with large, breaking waves of 5-8 ft. A 
strong southward-flowing longshore current will also be present. 
Expect minor coastal flooding along the Volusia coast and 
intracoastal waters. Residents and visitors should stay out of the 
dangerous surf.

Slight cooling and drier air are anticipated behind the recent 
front. Lows are forecast to dip into the 60s for the first time 
since June (see Climate section below for dates). Afternoon highs 
will be closer to or just below seasonal norms in the 80s.

Sat-Mon...Previous Modified...A generally pleasant weekend 
temperature and humidity-wise is on tap, especially in the mornings 
and evenings, but beach and marine conditions will remain poor to 
hazardous. The low pressure system over the Eastern Seaboard will
lift closer to the New England coast and become cutoff (nearly 
stationary), but far enough away from Florida for the pressure 
gradient to loosen as a weakening surface high drops into the 
Southeast, and the Bermuda high ridge axis begins to reach back 
towards the Caribbean. Northerly winds could still pick up to 
10-15 mph with gusts to 25 mph Sat, mainly along the coast, then 
become light while veering onshore through the rest of the period.
While winds are forecast to diminish, significant beach and 
marine hazards will linger on. Residents and visitors should be 
extra attentive to the forecast, as the surf may look more 
inviting during the weekend but rip current/surf hazards will 
still be present.

Morning lows will continue to be cooler and in the 60s and 
afternoon highs warming into the 80s with conditions mostly dry. 
Can't completely rule out ISOLD (less than 20%) onshore-moving 
showers and greatest threat along the Treasure Coast for this.

Tue-Wed...Previous Modified...Model solutions begin to diverge later 
into the extended. All the global models vary slightly in timing and 
location of a mid-upper level trough and associated surface low 
swinging across the CONUS, bringing the attendant surface front 
towards Florida mid to late next week. Prior to that, Florida 
remains under the influence of persistent troughing over the eastern 
seaboard and surface high pressure in the western Atlantic. There is 
some disagreement in the exact location of the surface ridge axis, 
but fairly confident low-level flow will remain onshore, just a 
question of whether it will be more ERLY or SERLY. There is less 
certainty how moisture will recover, with a fair spread between 
PWATs ticking up to near to below normal or surging back to above 
normal; decreasing confidence in forecast rain chances and heat 
impacts. As a result, official forecast calls for broadly
increasing rain chances from near/below normal Tue, becoming 
near/above normal Wed, with the return of lightning storm chances.
Temperatures tick up a few degrees becoming seasonably warm again
in the M-U80s, but additional moisture may cause heat indices to 
jump back into the 90s.
